title: A recording opens on a sharp first frame
goal: When a recording opens in the editor, the picture at the start is drawn blurred, like a small thumbnail stretched up, and stays that way until the playhead moves. It is the first thing anybody sees of their recording.
notes: Reproduced 2026-09-25 while building the video guides: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/tutorial-cut-a-recording-down-walk.json (probe, Next defaults, Screen Recording granted, screen unlocked). 1-a-clip-on-v1-sc.png at 0:00, after a 1s wait: the Ready card and the 0 counter are visibly blurred. 6-throw-a-piece-away-sc.png at 0:02 in the same run is sharp. The same blur shows at 0:00 in tutorial-put-a-transition-on-a-cut-walk (two clips, no trim fast lane) and tutorial-add-a-second-clip-walk, so it is not the Trim tool. Suspect the frame fetched at open (EditorState.openRecordingAsDocument -> documentMomentChanged) is a low-resolution one that is never replaced until the moment changes. Captures are copied in queue/audits/2026-09-25-video-guides-cut-sc.png.
acceptance: A recording opened at Next defaults shows its first frame as sharp as any later frame, without the playhead being moved
A walk photographs the picture at 0:00 right after opening and fails if it is blurred
Holds for a recording opened from the Finder and for one a guide opens

Picked up the previous attempt's stash. Reproduced before trusting it: with the fetcher fix held back, a-recording-opens-sharp-walk FAILED (read 431 wide, shown 2160 wide, after 3s) and a-guide-recording-opens-sharp-walk FAILED (Tutorial Sample read 160 wide, shown 1280 wide). Cause: the first frame is asked for before the canvas fits its window (an eighth of the size); the fit's full-size ask was skipped because that small read was still under way, so the small one was filed and drawn until the playhead moved. Fix: MovieFrameReads (PhotonzCore, tested) lets a bigger ask start its own read and never lets a smaller landing replace a bigger one; MovieFrameFetcher uses it. MovieFrames.swift is shared, so Current gets the fix too (a bug fix, not a Next feature). New walk step expectFrameSharp; added to the lock-safe list by reading, not watching (screen was unlocked), with a comment saying so.

Recordings now open sharp at 0:00. The fit's full-size read of the first frame was dropped while the small pre-fit read was in flight; MovieFrameReads (PhotonzCore, tested) now lets a bigger ask read again and never lets a smaller landing win. Reproduced first: both new walks (a-recording-opens-sharp-walk from the Finder, a-guide-recording-opens-sharp-walk from a guide) failed without the fix and pass with it, Next defaults, real captures. Scripts/test.sh green (9854 tests); tutorial-cut, transition, second-clip, opens-to-watch and an-editing-session walks pass. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-25-sharp-first-frame.json. Commit 688177b1.
